reviews.title: Don’t use, allows scam ads
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app for 5 or six years, starting with my Apple Watch SE.  The free version had what I needed, hours asleep and heart rate, basic stuff.  Then a few years ago, they decided to start showing ads unless users upgraded.  Not something that I liked, but it’s a common business model for apps, and the ads weren’t intrusive, so I tolerated them.  For the last few weeks, though, the ads they’ve shown are downright scams.  Ads that claim my device is infected or needs a critical upgrade.  This is bad, means the company is desperate for money, just to do something that Apple Health does for free.  Stay far, far away from SleepWatch!

reviews.title: Not Tracking Sleep
reviews.text:
I used to get out of bed, and SleepWatch would immediately ask to rate my sleep. Then I get all the information I needed. 
I recently learned that if you don’t get that request, the app will not give you a sleep readout.  So I manually activated the app, hoping it would trigger a readout, but it never asked me to rate my sleep.
The rating request only triggered when I manually recorded sleep hours, but then it gave a readout for the other metrics that made no sense at all. I’ve considered looking for another app.

reviews.title: Sleep algorithms problem

This app produces results that are sometimes so different from the others that it is almost comic. The others produce results that make more sense - with similar outcomes. Last night is a perfect example. SleepWatch “detected” 8 hours and 45 minutes of sleep. Apple Health and the bed AI tracker report 6 hours and 45 minutes of sleep. These latter results fit how last night felt for me.
